newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WTO to set panel in U.S.-EU grain trade dispute.
newsitem.headline: WTO to set panel in U.S.-EU grain trade dispute.

text.p: The World Trade Organisation will next week set up a panel to determine whether the European Union is violating open trade rules with a grain tariff system introduced last year, trade officials said.
The officials said the panel had been requested by the United States -- after a year of apparently fruitless talks with the EU on the system, which is based on a reference price.

Washington, which argues that the system violates agreements in the 1986-93 Uruguay Round of world trade negotiations, first asked for a panel in October 1995 but Brussels invoked its right to insist on further consultations.
EU officials said at the time that efforts were already being made to find a solution and that there was a good chance of a successful outcome without resort to a panel.
But trade diplomats said on Monday although talks had continued intermittently over the past year they had brought no agreement.

Under WTO rules, the three-member panel will be set up automatically when the trade watchdog's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) meets on December 3. A member country which is the target of a complaint can only block creation of a panel once.
Following the decision, the expert team must be set up within 30 days and then has six months to return its findings, which are subject to review by an appellate body if either side requests it.

The EU system is applied to imports of wheat, rye, barley, corn, sorghum and rice. The United States had argued that tariffs should be fixed on a consignment-by-consignment basis rather than on price reference.
